title: Which MongoDB CDC tool fits you?

questions.q: Who should run the change reader?
questions.hint: Almost every tool here reads MongoDB's change streams, so the choice is who runs the reader.

questions.q: What kinds of collections do you have?

options.label: Time series collections or views too
options.why: the manual says time series collections do not support change streams, and AWS DMS does not migrate them

native.name: Native change streams
native.summary: MongoDB's own change stream API, which most other tools here wrap.
native.bestWhen: an app needs to react to events, like sending an email on sign-up.
native.watchOut: you store resume tokens, handle retries and cope with schema changes yourself, and time series collections are not supported.

debezium.name: Debezium
debezium.summary: A free connector that wraps change streams and runs on Kafka Connect or as Debezium Server. The MongoDB Kafka connector is MongoDB's own alternative.
debezium.bestWhen: you already run Kafka and want one stream to feed many consumers.
debezium.watchOut: you run it yourself, and the Apache Iceberg sink for Debezium Server is community-maintained in a separate repository.

airbyte.name: Airbyte
airbyte.summary: A certified MongoDB source using change streams, with Core free to self-manage and a Cloud option.
airbyte.bestWhen: scheduled syncs are fine and you want a self-host option.
airbyte.watchOut: the default Lookup mode can hide steps between quick updates, and Post Image mode needs MongoDB 6.0 or later with images turned on.

fivetran.name: Fivetran
fivetran.summary: A vendor-run connector that copies existing data, then switches to change streams.
fivetran.bestWhen: you want someone else to run it and a warehouse is the goal.
fivetran.watchOut: deleted documents stay as rows flagged with _fivetran_deleted, and nested data stays as JSON.

estuary.name: Estuary
estuary.summary: A vendor-run connector with a change stream mode and two batch modes.
estuary.bestWhen: you want continuous capture and need views or time series collections too.
estuary.watchOut: only the change stream mode captures deletes, and Iceberg tables need Spark for merging or only append delta updates.

dms.name: AWS DMS
dms.summary: A managed service in your AWS account with document and table modes.
dms.bestWhen: your sources and targets already sit in AWS.
dms.watchOut: Iceberg is not a target endpoint, table mode needs one type per field, and the task fails if the oplog is flushed too early.

striim.name: Striim
striim.summary: An enterprise tool that reads change streams on MongoDB 4.2 or later and the oplog before that.
striim.bestWhen: MongoDB is one of many enterprise sources.
striim.watchOut: the default mode loads existing data and stops, so you must set Incremental, and its Iceberg Writer is Google Cloud Storage only (S3 Tables has its own writer).

olake.name: OLake Go
olake.summary: Free software that copies MongoDB changes into Apache Iceberg or Parquet on your own storage, with no Kafka. With the Horizon catalog it can also create Iceberg tables in Snowflake.
olake.bestWhen: you want MongoDB changes in Iceberg tables you control, without Kafka.
olake.watchOut: output goes to Iceberg or Parquet on storage you choose, and CDC runs when your orchestrator starts a job.
